title: Prefect Overview

definition.content:
## Prefect

Prefect is a Python-first workflow orchestration platform used to schedule and execute flows and tasks across work pools, work queues, and workers. This dashboard follows the orchestration path top-down: control-plane health, work queue backlog and polling, worker and work pool capacity, flow run reliability and load, flow run latency, and task-level drilldown.

Events require `collect_events: true` in the check configuration.

- [Datadog Prefect integration documentation](https://docs.datadoghq.com/integrations/prefect/)
- [Prefect product page](https://www.prefect.io/)
Key health and activity signals at a glance for quick detection of problems and drill-down into the relevant section.

Where work is piling up and which queues are falling behind. Use backlog size and age to prioritize intervention, last polled age to catch stalled consumers, and concurrency in use to find queues throttled by their own limits.
Execution capacity behind the queues. Confirm each work pool has online workers and is ready and unpaused, then rank workers by heartbeat age to find lost or stale workers before queues starve.

Demand and outcomes of scheduled work. Compare runs started against terminal outcomes, watch in-flight state counts for load, and rank deployments by failures and late starts to see where to intervene.

definition.title: Late starts by deployment and queue

definition.content: Where a delayed flow run spent its time. Split latency into queue wait before start, execution time, and gaps between retries, then rank deployments by tail execution time to catch regressions against their SLO.

Drill down from a slow or failing flow to the tasks responsible. Compare task outcomes and duration trends, then rank task keys by tail execution time, upstream dependency wait, and failures to shorten the critical path.
Prefect server and worker logs, with error-level entries surfaced first for correlation with failed or crashed runs.

definition.title: Error logs
